statement: The cross-entropy $H(p, q)$ between two probability distributions $p$ and $q$ over discrete events is defined as $H(p, q) = -\sum_{m} p_m \log q_m$.

symbols.meaning: cross-entropy between probability distributions p and q
probability of event m under distribution p
probability of event m under distribution q

properties.property: When comparing distribution q against a fixed reference distribution p, minimizing cross-entropy H(p, q) with respect to q is equivalent to minimizing the Kullback-Leibler divergence D_KL(p || q), attaining its minimum value H(p) when p = q.
properties.why: Cross-entropy and KL divergence are identical up to the additive constant H(p) when p is fixed, and Gibbs' inequality shows both are minimized at p = q

properties.property: Maximizing the empirical likelihood L(theta; x) of an i.i.d. sample under model q_theta is equivalent to minimizing the cross-entropy H(p, q_theta).
properties.why: Taking the logarithm gives log L(theta; x) = -N * H(p, q_theta), and the logarithm is a monotonically increasing function

properties.property: For a binary classification task where p in {y, 1 - y} and q in {y_hat, 1 - y_hat}, the cross-entropy evaluates to the binary log loss H(p, q) = -y log(y_hat) - (1 - y) log(1 - y_hat).
properties.why: Evaluating the definition -sum_m p_m log q_m across the two outcome classes {0, 1}

properties.property: For logistic regression parameterized by weights w with y_hat_i = g(w . X^i), the gradient of the total cross-entropy loss L(w) is nabla_w L(w) = X^T (y_hat - y).
properties.why: The derivative of the logistic function simplifies each partial derivative dL/dw_j to sum_{i=1}^N X_ij (y_hat_i - y_i)

assumptions.assumption: The distributions p and q share the same event space, with q_m > 0 whenever p_m > 0.
assumptions.breaks_when: The predicted model assigns probability q_m = 0 to an outcome where p_m > 0, causing log(q_m) to be undefined (-infinity).

assumptions.assumption: The reference distribution p is fixed when treating cross-entropy minimization as equivalent to KL divergence minimization.
assumptions.breaks_when: The reference distribution q is fixed and p is optimized, making H(p, q) minimization and D_KL(p || q) minimization non-equivalent because H(p) varies.

failure_modes.mode: Zero predicted probability on a positive-probability event
failure_modes.signature: Cross-entropy loss diverges to infinity or produces numerical NaN/overflow in gradient computation.
failure_modes.cause: Evaluation of log(q_m) when q_m = 0 for an event with p_m > 0.

failure_modes.mode: Non-equivalence between cross-entropy and relative entropy minimization under varying reference
failure_modes.signature: Optimizing p to approximate a fixed prior q yields a different optimal distribution than minimizing KL divergence.
failure_modes.cause: Cross-entropy H(p, q) differs from D_KL(p || q) by the entropy H(p), which is not constant when p is being optimized.
